<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world puzzle adventure in a modern dystopian city, where the character completes missions to escape and find paradise outside.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions and finish without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport at most 1280px wide) for visual checks, and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js city adventure with procedural geometry, story missions, relay puzzles, optional memory fragments, keyboard/mouse and touch controls, and an ending.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game interface, responsive styling, and gameplay implementation in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` completed without output.
- Started a local HTTP server at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright opened the page.

### Active
- Validate the game in-browser, check console errors, capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot, and fix any issues discovered.

### Blocked
- Browser opened with “Console: 1 errors, 4 warnings”; the cause has not yet been inspected.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `playwright-cli console` and resolve any gameplay/runtime errors.
2. Start the game in-browser and verify movement, interactions, puzzle progression, and ending.
3. Save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
4. Summarize the finished game and note assumptions briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface, HUD, mission/puzzle/help/ending screens, and Three.js entry point.
- `game.js`: World generation, controls, objectives, interaction logic, puzzles, and game loop.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The game loads Three.js 0.166.1 via `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.166.1/build/three.module.js`.
- Playwright’s first open attempt failed because Chromium was not installed; `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` succeeded.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a playable 3D open-world puzzle adventure in a dystopian city, where the character completes missions to escape and find paradise outside.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions and finish without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js adventure with procedural city geometry, story missions, relay puzzles, optional memory fragments, keyboard/mouse and touch controls, and an ending.
- Instanced building windows to reduce scene draw calls after movement testing showed little progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game interface, responsive styling, objectives, puzzles, and gameplay in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added an objective update when the player reaches the archive, and a data-URL favicon to prevent the browser’s favicon 404.
- `node --check game.js` passes; browser console is clear after reload.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/outside-current.jpg` at a 1280px-wide viewport.

- Re-capture and inspect the latest JPEG after fixes and gameplay validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Diagnose why keyboard movement barely changes the objective distance during Playwright testing.
2. Verify archive access, solve relay sequences, and confirm the ending is reachable.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; check the browser console again.
4. Summarize the finished game and key assumptions.

Implemented the requested overhaul.

### HUD and direction
- Mission directive now starts minimized and no longer covers the play area.
- Added a directional arrow that rotates toward the current objective.
- Click the `＋` button or press `M` to expand/collapse it.
- `Esc` releases the mouse so interface buttons can be clicked; puzzles and conversations also release it automatically.

### Buildings and interiors
- All city buildings now have solid collision volumes.
- Enterable buildings have real door gaps; walls remain impassable.
- Added two enterable locations:
  - **Transit Archive** — archive terminal puzzle and Mara, the archive keeper.
  - **The Signal House** — Relay 02 puzzle and Pell, an injured courier.
- Added camera wall avoidance so the third-person camera does not sit outside interior walls.

### World detail
- Added 14 trash cans, some tipped, with trash bags.
- Added seven neon signs, including:
  - `TRANSIT ARCHIVE`
  - `THE SIGNAL HOUSE`
  - `NOODLE 24H`
  - `SLEEP PODS`
  - `FIX / BODY`
  - `NIGHT MARKET`
  - `OPEN`
- Added two burning barrel fires.
- Added six interactive NPCs, including displaced, injured, and nearly dead characters:
  - Mara, Pell, Sable, Ren, Noma, and Kesh.
- Conversations use a new dialogue panel with multi-line lore, progressing with `E` or the Continue button.
- NPC nameplates now scale with distance and hide during conversations.

### Validation
- Full mission flow validated through archive pass, all three relays, and the ending.
- Door-gap and solid-wall collision checks passed.
- Mobile/desktop layouts checked.
- Final smoke test completed with no console errors.

## Objective
- Complete and refine the playable 3D open-world dystopian city adventure, including enterable buildings, richer city life, varied puzzles, and the route beyond the perimeter.

## Requirements
- Keep the mission directive compact and collapsible while preserving its objective arrow.
- Keep buildings solid and allow entry only through usable, lit doors.
- Add distinct interiors, character detail, fog, city lights, responsive camera controls, and an accurate minimap.
- Populate the city with varied NPCs and roaming cats, dogs, and crows.
- Add varied puzzles while preserving the established relay answers and ending route.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use solid building collision volumes and a `.42` player collision radius.
- Use `E` for interactions and dialogue; Escape closes interfaces or releases mouse lock.
- Preserve archive `[MID, LOW, HUSH]`, relay 01 `[LOW, HIGH, HUSH]`, relay 02 `[MID, HUSH, LOW]`, and relay 03 `[HIGH, MID, LOW]`.
- Player starts at `(0, 0, 15)`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the Three.js city, mission flow, dialogue, puzzles, pass collection, gate opening, and outside ending.
- Added solid building collisions, Archive and Signal House entrances/interiors, compact mission card, street clutter, neon signs, fog, lights, and camera wall avoidance.
- Added NPC lore/dialogue and nameplates.
- Added enterable supermarket, police office, post office, and house interiors with themed fixtures, lighting, and signs.
- Added eight NPCs and roaming cats, dogs, and crows.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Local HTTP server was launched for port `3002`; the shell command timed out after starting, but reported no output.

### Active
- Validate new buildings, animal motion, and NPCs in a live browser.
- Improve character geometry and minimap/player-arrow alignment.
- Add a puzzle format beyond the existing tone-sequence puzzles.
- Rerun route, collision, puzzle, dialogue, desktop, and mobile smoke tests.

### Blocked
- Browser validation and screenshot of the latest changes have not been confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002` and verify the latest changes render without console errors.
2. Check building access/collision and interior fixtures; verify NPC placement and animal movement.
3. Continue the remaining character, minimap, and puzzle improvements.
4. Rerun the full mission-route and responsive smoke tests.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World generation, interiors, NPCs, animals, puzzles, movement, camera, minimap, and game loop.
- `index.html`: HUD, dialogue, puzzle, map, start/help, and ending screens.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and interface styling.

## Important Context
- Relay solutions: `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`; archive solution `[1,0,3]`.
- Three.js `0.166.1` is loaded from jsDelivr.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete and refine the playable 3D dystopian city adventure, including enterable buildings, city life, varied puzzles, and the route beyond the perimeter.

## Requirements
- Keep the mission directive compact and collapsible while preserving its objective arrow.
- Keep buildings solid; allow entry only through usable, lit doors.
- Add distinct interiors, character detail, fog, city lights, responsive camera controls, and an accurate minimap.
- Populate the city with varied NPCs and roaming cats, dogs, and crows.
- Add varied puzzles while preserving relay answers and the ending route.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use solid building collision volumes and a `.42` player collision radius.
- Use `E` for interactions and dialogue; Escape closes interfaces or releases mouse lock.
- Preserve archive `[MID, LOW, HUSH]`, relay 01 `[LOW, HIGH, HUSH]`, relay 02 `[MID, HUSH, LOW]`, and relay 03 `[HIGH, MID, LOW]`.
- Player starts at `(0, 0, 15)`.
- Move the Transit Archive to the north edge of the Low Quarter at `(-27, 14)`; its east door is lit.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the Three.js city, mission flow, dialogue, puzzles, pass collection, gate opening, and outside ending.
- Added building collisions, multiple themed enterable interiors, street details, neon signs, fog, lighting, and camera wall avoidance.
- Added NPC lore/nameplates, eight NPCs, and roaming cats, dogs, and crows.
- Added mobile minimap pinning CSS and moved the Archive, its interior fixtures, door light, NPC, and location label.

## Objective
- Refine the existing playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world with richer interiors and connected chapter themes.
- Improve animal behavior, minimap controls, NPC variety, traffic, and story-connected puzzles.

## Requirements
- Birds should walk, peck at trash, visibly flap, and immediately fly away when the player approaches; show clear head, beak, wings, tail, and eyes.
- Cats should have four legs, ears, eyes, snouts, tails, varied colors, wall-avoiding random paths, and a petting interaction with visible reactions.
- Make the minimap smaller, put it in the top-right corner, and allow minimizing/maximizing it.
- Give human NPCs distinct clothes, hairstyles, and eyes, plus varied movement during interactions.
- Use a more 3D anime-like style for the player, NPCs, and world; increase city fog.
- Add randomly placed parked cars that block player movement.
- Make interiors more complex and congested.
- Connect puzzles to the story; center Chapter 1 on lower-class life, Chapter 2 on middle-class life, and Chapter 3 on wealthy/high-class life.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Preserve the established mission route, relay answers, ending, and solid building collision.
- Use a shared cel-shading ramp and toon materials to extend the anime look across world geometry.
- Keep parked cars within selected road slots and add them to collision handling.
- Preserve the archive’s established placement and east-side lit door.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main game route, puzzles, and ending; the earlier end-to-end route test reached the final route stages.
- Added NPCs and roaming animals, themed enterable interiors, building collision, fog, lighting, and camera collision avoidance.
- Applied toon shading to core world materials and building/interior materials; adjusted interior camera height and added building roofs.
- Refined cat geometry and rebuilt the bird with visible body parts and flapping wings.
- Added interior dressing and congested room details; added a small number of randomly selected parked-car slots.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the latest code edits; an earlier browser pass reported `errors []`.

### Active
- Validate bird flight/pecking/flee behavior, cat navigation and petting, NPC interaction animation, vehicle collisions, interior access/density, and the final visual changes in a live browser.
- Implement or verify the requested minimap size, top-right placement, and minimize/maximize controls.
- Ensure story and puzzle content clearly reinforce the three chapter class perspectives.

### Blocked
- No known blocker; latest browser run and final route/responsive checks are not confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` to verify which requested features are implemented and address any gaps, especially minimap controls and story/puzzle linkage.
2. Run syntax checks and browser tests for animal behavior, pet interaction, NPC variety, car/building collisions, interior placement, and mobile/desktop map behavior.
3. Rerun the full mission route and leave all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World rendering, animals, NPCs, interiors, cars, puzzles, mission flow, movement, and minimap logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, dialogue, puzzle, map, start/help, and ending interfaces.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and map positioning.

## Important Context
- Relay solutions: `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`; archive solution: `[1,0,3]`.
- Player starts at `(0, 0, 15)`; the Transit Archive is at `(-27, 14)` with its east door lit.
- Latest edits are uncommitted.

- Refine the existing playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world with richer interiors and connected chapter themes.

## Requirements
- Birds should walk and peck at trash, visibly flap, and immediately fly away when the player approaches; show clear head, beak, wings, tail, and eyes.
- Cats should have four legs, ears, eyes, snouts, tails, varied colors, wall-avoiding random paths, and a petting interaction with visible reactions.
- Make the minimap smaller, top-right, and minimizable/maximizable.
- Give human NPCs distinct clothes, hairstyles, and eyes, plus varied movement during interactions.
- Make the player, NPCs, and world more 3D anime-like; increase city fog.
- Add randomly placed parked cars that block player movement.
- Make interiors more complex and congested.
- Connect puzzles to the story; center Chapter 1 on lower-class life, Chapter 2 on middle-class life, and Chapter 3 on wealthy/high-class life.
- Preserve the established mission route, relay answers, ending, solid building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Keep parked cars within selected road slots and include them in collision handling.
- Preserve the established mission route and story-critical puzzle answers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main game route, puzzles, and ending; an earlier end-to-end route test reached the final route stages.
- Added NPCs, roaming animals, themed enterable interiors, building collision, fog, lighting, and camera collision avoidance.
- Applied toon shading to core world, building, and interior materials; adjusted interior camera height and added building roofs.
- Refined cat geometry and rebuilt the bird with visible body parts and flapping wings.
- Added interior dressing and congested room details, plus randomly selected parked-car slots.
- `node --check game.js` passed after latest code edits; an earlier browser pass reported `errors []`.
- Most recent inspection confirmed `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are modified and uncommitted.

### Active
- Inspect and implement or verify minimap size, top-right placement, and minimize/maximize controls.
- Validate bird flight, pecking, and flee behavior; cat navigation and petting; NPC interaction animation; vehicle/building collisions; and interior access/density in a live browser.
- Verify story and puzzle content clearly reinforce the three chapter class perspectives.
- Rerun the full mission route and desktop/mobile map checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` for remaining minimap and story/puzzle gaps.
2. Run syntax checks and live-browser tests for animals, interactions, collisions, interiors, and responsive map behavior.
3. Rerun the full mission route and leave all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World rendering, animals, NPCs, interiors, cars, puzzles, mission flow, movement, and minimap logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, dialogue, puzzle, map, start/help, and ending interfaces.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and map positioning.

## Important Context
- Relay solutions: `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`; archive solution: `[1,0,3]`.
- Player starts at `(0, 0, 15)`; the Transit Archive is at `(-27, 14)` with its east door lit.

Potential issue: when inside, camera behind the player may be on other side of a wall, showing outside. Clamp by collider sampling to avoid. Good.

## Objective
- Refine the existing playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world with richer interiors and connected chapter themes.

## Requirements
- Birds should walk and peck at trash, visibly flap, and immediately fly away when the player approaches; show clear head, beak, wings, tail, and eyes.
- Cats should have four legs, ears, eyes, snouts, tails, varied colors, wall-avoiding random paths, and a petting interaction with visible reactions.
- Make the minimap smaller, top-right, and minimizable/maximizable.
- Give human NPCs distinct clothes, hairstyles, and eyes, plus varied movement during interactions.
- Make the player, NPCs, and world more 3D anime-like; increase city fog.
- Add randomly placed parked cars that block player movement.
- Make interiors more complex and congested.
- Connect puzzles to the story; center Chapter 1 on lower-class life, Chapter 2 on middle-class life, and Chapter 3 on wealthy/high-class life.
- Preserve the established mission route, relay answers, ending, solid building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Keep parked cars within selected road slots and include them in collision handling.
- Preserve the established mission route and story-critical puzzle answers.

## Objective
- Refine the existing playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world with richer interiors and chapters centered on distinct social classes.

## Requirements
- Birds should walk and peck at trash, visibly flap, and immediately fly away when the player approaches; show clear head, beak, wings, tail, and eyes.
- Cats should have four legs, ears, eyes, snouts, tails, varied colors, wall-avoiding random paths, and a petting interaction with visible reactions.
- Make the minimap smaller, top-right, and minimizable/maximizable.
- Give human NPCs distinct clothes, hairstyles, and eyes, plus varied movement during interactions.
- Make the player, NPCs, and world more 3D anime-like; increase city fog.
- Add randomly placed parked cars that block player movement.
- Make interiors more complex and congested.
- Connect puzzles to the story; center Chapter 1 on lower-class life, Chapter 2 on middle-class life, and Chapter 3 on wealthy/high-class life.
- Preserve the established mission route, relay answers, ending, solid building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Keep parked cars within selected road slots and include them in collision handling.
- Preserve the established mission route and story-critical puzzle answers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main game route, puzzles, and ending; an earlier end-to-end route test reached the final route stages.
- Added NPCs, roaming animals, themed enterable interiors, building collision, fog, lighting, and camera collision avoidance.
- Applied toon shading to core world, building, and interior materials; adjusted interior camera height and added building roofs.
- Refined cat geometry and rebuilt the bird with visible body parts and flapping wings.
- Added interior dressing and congested room details, plus randomly selected parked-car slots.
- Added top-right minimap controls; `index.html` has a 140×140 canvas and minimize button, with toggle logic in `game.js`.
- Added varied NPC interaction animation; `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are modified and uncommitted.
- `node --check game.js` passed after latest code edits; an earlier browser pass reported `errors []`.

### Active
- Validate bird flight, pecking, and flee behavior; cat navigation and petting; NPC interaction animation; vehicle/building collisions; and interior access/density in a live browser.
- Verify story and puzzle content clearly reinforce the three chapter class perspectives.
- Confirm minimap sizing, top-right placement, and minimize/maximize behavior on desktop and mobile.
- Rerun the full mission route.
- Continue examining interior selection and animation/dialogue flow in `game.js`; recent inspections covered `interiorAt`, `archiveHouse`, `interiors`, `animate`, and `dialogueOpen`, but no test results or fixes were recorded.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect remaining implementation gaps in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
2. Run syntax checks and live-browser tests for animals, interactions, collisions, interiors, and responsive minimap behavior.
3. Rerun the full mission route and leave all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World rendering, animals, NPCs, interiors, cars, puzzles, mission flow, movement, and minimap logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, dialogue, puzzle, map, start/help, and ending interfaces.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and map positioning.

- Relay solutions: `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`; archive solution: `[1,0,3]`.

- Refine the existing playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world with richer interiors and chapters centered on distinct social classes.
- Address the latest requests for usable drag-to-look controls, natural animal/NPC animations, collision fixes, richer interiors and exteriors, animated chapter gates, and dystopian audio.

## Requirements
- Make drag-to-look usable; fix the interior view where walls appear transparent to the outside.
- Give walking birds natural foot animation; retain visible anatomy and flee behavior.
- Add exterior furnishings and more interior detail; prevent interior props from overlapping.
- Give NPCs varied activities and movement; add a backpack to the player character.
- Prevent players from passing through exterior props such as trash cans; make burning-bin flames look natural.
- Add large animated chapter gates with nearby levers accessible only after required puzzles are solved.
- Add dystopian background music and sound effects for NPC dialogue, fire, lights, birds, and machinery.
- Preserve the established mission route, relay answers, ending, solid building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Keep parked cars within selected road slots and include them in collision handling.
- Preserve story-critical puzzle answers: relay solutions `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`; archive solution `[1,0,3]`.
- Move the Meridian checkpoint to `(4.8, 13.4)` to avoid conflict with the chapter gate; put its lever on the gate’s west side and add collider handling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing route, puzzles, ending, NPCs, animals, enterable interiors, collision, fog, lighting, and minimap controls are in place from earlier work.
- Added colliders for tipped trash cans, Meridian checkpoint, and gate levers; adjusted some parked-car and interior prop positions.
- Removed pointer-lock request from the start action.
- Added interior lamp shades, expanded interior furnishings/details, revised wall-frame placement, and increased decorative detail counts.
- Reworked burning-bin flames with layered shapes, glow, coals, and embers; expanded chapter gate panels and gate wings.
- Bird feet now use separate foot groups to support more natural stepping.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest bird-foot edit; browser inspection earlier reported no runtime exceptions, and the archive wall material was opaque (`transparent:false`, `opacity:1`, `depthWrite:true`).
- All modifications remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Fix and verify drag-to-look; the latest change only removed pointer-lock initiation and does not establish that dragging works.
- Investigate and fix the interior wall/outside-view issue; material opacity was checked, but the visual issue remains unverified/resolved.
- Verify bird foot animation after the recent foot-group change.
- Add the player backpack and confirm NPC activity animations.
- Verify prop collision and interior furnishing overlaps in a live browser.
- Verify gate opening animations and puzzle/lever access conditions.
- Confirm dystopian music and requested sound effects are implemented and working.
- Rerun syntax checks and the full mission route.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect pointer/mouse/touch look handlers and implement reliable drag-to-look without relying on pointer lock.
2. Recheck interior visibility/camera clipping and repair the reported transparent-wall appearance.
3. Finish the backpack and validate the recent bird-foot, NPC activity, collision, furnishing, gate, and audio changes in-browser.
4. Run `node --check game.js`, inspect browser errors, and replay the full mission route while keeping changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, camera/look controls, animals, NPCs, interiors, props, collisions, gates, audio, puzzles, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: HUD and game interfaces, including minimap controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and minimap positioning.

## Important Context
- Player starts at `(0, 0, 15)`; Transit Archive is at `(-27, 14)` with its east door lit.
- Chapter gates are at `z=10` and `z=-22`; perimeter gate is near `z=-72`.
- The last recorded syntax check preceded the latest bird-foot edit; rerun it before browser testing.

## Objective
- Refine the playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world, then verify all gameplay and visual systems.

## Requirements
- Make drag-to-look reliable across mouse and touch layouts.
- Prevent interior walls or exterior views from appearing transparent through the camera.
- Preserve walking-bird foot animation, anatomy, and flee behavior.
- Add exterior furnishings and detailed interiors without prop overlap or player prop passage.
- Add natural burning-bin flames and a player backpack.
- Add large animated chapter gates with puzzle-gated, accessible levers.
- Add dystopian music and sound effects for NPC dialogue, fire, lights, birds, and machinery.
- Preserve mission route, relay answers `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`, archive answer `[1,0,3]`, ending, building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep parked cars in road slots and in collision handling.
- Keep modifications uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use drag-to-look as the primary control with no pointer-lock requirement.
- Move the Meridian checkpoint to `(4.8, 13.4)` and place its lever on the gate’s west side.
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Start vertical drag using conventional reverse direction.
- Keep the archive at `(-27, 14)` and the east door lit.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented drag-to-look on the canvas for mouse and touch with pointer capture.
- Updated indoor camera clamping to keep the camera inside rooms and away from walls.
- Added player backpack, varied NPC and animal animation, interiors, furnishings, gate mechanics, and audio systems.
- Preserved relay, archive, mission, collision, parked-car, gate, lever, and ending logic.
- Running `node --check game.js` passes.
- Verified the start scene renders in Chromium with SwiftShader and no page/script errors.

### Active
- Complete browser interaction verification for drag-to-look.
- Inspect the archive interior and other interiors for wall transparency.
- Verify bird feet, NPC activity animation, backpack, prop collision, prop overlap, gates, and audio.
- Replay the full mission route and inspect browser errors.

### Blocked
- Automated browser click verification is currently blocked by Playwright timing out while clicking `#start-button`.
- Full in-browser verification remains incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Run Chromium interaction tests using the system executable and obtain a reliable start action.
2. Verify yaw/pitch change after mouse and touch-style canvas drags.
3. Teleport or navigate to `(-27, 14)` and inspect interior screenshots for wall transparency.
4. Replay all puzzles and gates using the preserved solutions.
5. Verify birds, NPCs, prop collisions, backpack, gates, audio, and final route, then rerun `node --check game.js`.
6. Keep all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Camera, controls, world, interiors, NPCs, animals, gates, collision, puzzles, audio, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, start screen, controls, and UI layering.
- `style.css`: Canvas/UI stacking, touch behavior, responsive layout.
- `screenshots/after-drag-fix.png`: Chromium start-scene capture.
- `screenshots/archive-interior.png`: Intended archive validation capture, not yet produced.

## Important Context
- The drag patch is attached to `canvas#game`, not the shell overlay.
- Interior camera logic now clamps to room bounds and rejects positions colliding with wall colliders.
- Automated capture should use `/usr/bin/chromium` with SwiftShader; the Playwright CLI cannot currently find its bundled browser.
- No changes are committed.

## Objective
- Refine the playable 3D dystopian city adventure into a more anime-styled, lively world, then verify its gameplay and visual systems.
- Improve rendering performance without changing the mission or puzzle logic.

## Requirements
- Make drag-to-look reliable across mouse and touch, with no pointer-lock requirement.
- Prevent interior walls or exterior views from appearing transparent through the camera.
- Preserve bird foot animation, anatomy, and flee behavior; add lively NPC activity.
- Add exterior furnishings and detailed interiors without prop overlap or player passage through props.
- Add natural burning-bin flames, a player backpack, animated chapter gates, and accessible puzzle-gated levers.
- Add dystopian music and sound effects for NPC dialogue, fire, lights, birds, and machinery.
- Preserve mission route, relay answers `[0,2,3]`, `[1,3,0]`, `[2,1,0]`, archive answer `[1,0,3]`, ending, building collision, archive placement, and east-side lit door.
- Keep parked cars in road slots and include them in collision handling.
- Keep modifications uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Use drag-to-look as the primary control; start vertical drag in the conventional reverse direction.
- Place the Meridian checkpoint at `(4.8, 13.4)` with its lever on the gate’s west side.
- Use shared cel-shading and toon materials across world geometry.
- Keep the archive at `(-27, 14)` and the east door lit.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented canvas mouse/touch drag-to-look with pointer capture and indoor camera clamping.
- Added the previously requested backpack, NPC/animal animation, interiors, furnishings, gates, levers, and audio systems.
- Added toon-material caching, static world geometry batching, adaptive render resolution, and reduced DPR caps.
- Fixed a batching-time `computeBoundingSphere` issue by computing it on the merged geometry.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Chromium runs produced `screenshots/opt-start.png`, `screenshots/opt-archive.png`, and `screenshots/opt-gateA.png`.

### Active
- Finish checking archive/interior lighting and wall transparency; the latest inspection focused on `interiorLamp`, `pendantLamp`, and nearby point-light setup.
- Confirm performance batching does not break dynamic objects or visual/gameplay behavior.
- Complete mission route, drag input, collision, prop overlap, audio, and final-route verification.

### Blocked
- No current blocker recorded; full verification remains incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Inspect archive and other interior screenshots; resolve any lighting or wall-transparency defects.
2. Confirm static batching leaves animated objects intact and evaluate performance at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
3. Verify mouse and touch drag-to-look changes yaw/pitch.
4. Replay the mission with the preserved puzzle answers and check gates, collisions, props, birds, NPCs, audio, and ending.
5. Rerun `node --check game.js` and keep all changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, controls, interiors, materials, batching, performance, puzzles, collision, audio, and mission logic.
- `index.html`: UI and Three.js import map.
- `style.css`: Canvas/UI stacking, touch behavior, and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/opt-start.png`: Chromium start-scene capture after rendering changes.
- `screenshots/opt-archive.png`: Archive interior validation capture.
- `screenshots/opt-gateA.png`: Gate validation capture.

## Important Context
- `game.js` exposes `window.__dbg` for browser inspection, including `batchStats` and `perf`.
- Static batching skips objects marked `userData.dynamic`; verify dynamic content remains unaffected.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

Many examples set `light.shadow.camera.left = -50` and don't call updateProjectionMatrix... Actually the default `DirectionalLightShadow` camera has `updateProjectionMatrix` called in its constructor. If you change left/right after, you need `updateProjectionMatrix()`. ## Objective
- Minimize visual glitches and lag in the existing 3D city adventure without reducing its visual quality or changing its mission and puzzle logic.

## Requirements
- Preserve the game’s visual quality, mission route, puzzles, and gameplay behavior while improving smoothness and reducing glitches.
- Keep changes uncommitted.

## Decisions
- Batch static geometry and articulated character-part details to reduce draw calls while retaining animations and silhouettes.
- Use collision substeps to prevent movement tunneling during slow frames.
- Update HUD text less frequently; retain full render resolution and lighting quality rather than adaptive quality reduction.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added character-part batching for humans, birds, the cat, and backpack; static world batching remains in place.
- Added movement substeps and reused camera vectors to reduce tunneling and per-frame allocations.
- Kept shadow maps updating continuously; restored stronger lighting and higher DPR caps.
- Fixed dialogue blip timers so delayed callbacks do not access a cleared NPC.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser checks showed no runtime errors after the dialogue fix, and mouse drag changed yaw and pitch.
- Replayed archive and relay puzzles with the specified answers; objective progression and gates advanced.

### Active
- Diagnose and correct remaining visual glitches, especially unexpected darkness/black rendering in player and character close-ups after batching.
- Recheck performance and visuals after resolving the close-up rendering issue.

### Blocked
- Browser close-up screenshots of the player, NPC, and bird appeared predominantly black; the cause remains undetermined.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `batchPart` and merged character geometry/material transforms to identify the close-up rendering defect.
2. Re-run browser checks and inspect representative gameplay, character, archive, and gate views after fixing it.
3. Recheck drag-to-look, collision, puzzle progression, and runtime errors; keep changes uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Rendering, batching, controls, collision, dialogue, puzzles, and mission logic.
- `screenshots/closeup-player.png`: Player close-up showing the rendering issue.
- `screenshots/closeup-npc.png`: NPC close-up showing the rendering issue.
- `screenshots/closeup-bird.png`: Bird close-up showing the rendering issue.
- `screenshots/look-archive.png`: Archive view from a browser validation run.

## Important Context
- Latest browser run reported `base.calls: 684` at a 1024×576 viewport and no runtime errors; draw-call counts varied across camera positions.
- Earlier mission checks advanced archive and relay objectives successfully, but the final gate check was not conclusive.
- `window.__dbg` exposes scene, renderer, player, entities, birds, camera, yaw/pitch, and mission state for browser inspection.
